size.note: Newman's Birds gives about 45 cm. Southern African endemic; split from Mountain Buzzard B. oreophilus.

habitat: Montane plantations and forest or adjacent grassy plateaux; perches on the fringe of open areas (Newman's). Essentially absent from Kruger lowveld — rare/vagrant at best.
summary: An uncommon endemic forest buzzard, very similar to Steppe Buzzard. Somewhat smaller; dark brown above, white below with brown blotching; central breast usually white; flanks only blotched in immatures (Newman's).

similar.note: Steppe Buzzard is the common summer visitor; Forest is slightly smaller with a typically whiter central breast and forest/plantation habitat (Newman's). Extremely difficult; many records may be misidentified Steppe Buzzards (SABAP1).

research.note: Status is omitted. This is a rare visitor in Kruger, and the site has no vagrant status. The vocabulary is resident, intra-african-migrant, palearctic-migrant, and the older summer-migrant. No seasonal plumage change described. Gaps: Only 22 GBIF records in Kruger box — treat as rare visitor/vagrant. Flight photos not curated. Confusion with Steppe Buzzard undermines many historical records (SABAP1). Photos left out: A repeated file was omitted. Endemic. Split from Buteo oreophilus (Mountain Buzzard). Images from Hangklip Forest, Mpumalanga (not Kruger). monthsPresent set from Newman/SABAP seasonality cross-checked with GBIF Kruger month facets (not abundance). SABAP1 says it was thought sedentary but may be largely a nonbreeding migrant to the Transvaal, so status stays omitted.
